title: Your first assembly program

milestone.title: From Machine Code to Modern Languages

description:
Lesson 5.01's program printed a message with a system call. Change it to print exactly these two lines:

```
Assembly is machine code
with names.
```

and exit with code 0. Keep the `syscall` approach: put the bytes in the `.data` section with `db` (a new line is the number 10), work out their length with `equ $ - label`, and ask for system call 1 (write) and then 60 (exit).

starter.main.asm:
global  _start
        section .data
message: db     "Hello from assembly", 10
length  equ     $ - message

        section .text
_start:
        mov     eax, 1              ; system call 1: write
        mov     edi, 1              ; to standard output
        lea     rsi, [rel message]  ; these bytes
        mov     edx, length         ; this many of them
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60             ; system call 60: exit
        xor     edi, edi            ; with code 0
        syscall

solution.main.asm:
global  _start
        section .data
message: db     "Assembly is machine code", 10, "with names.", 10
length  equ     $ - message

        section .text
_start:
        mov     eax, 1
        mov     edi, 1
        lea     rsi, [rel message]
        mov     edx, length
        syscall

        mov     eax, 60
        xor     edi, edi
        syscall

rules: Print with a system call, as in the lesson.

examples.name: the message
examples.expected:
Assembly is machine code
with names.
